messages:
dan_customer: Hey team — our March invoice shows 2.3M tokens but the dashboard 'served tokens' is ~1.6M. Can you explain the gap? Our app didn't change, just a small rollout.

alice_support: Sorry for the trouble, dan. Can you paste a recent request id or an example cURL so we can trace?

dan_customer: Sure — one request id: req_20260312_9f3a. Example call: `curl -X POST https://api.redwood.ai/v1/generate -H \"Authorization: Bearer sk_...\" -d '{"model":"rw-large-16k","input":"summarize: ..."}'`

bob_billing: Thanks. Quick note: billing counts metered tokens (what ran on GPUs) which can differ from "served" tokens shown in the UI that reflect tokens returned to the client. We'll pull the metering logs for that req id.

obsbot: [ingest] trace req_20260312_9f3a -> routed to region:us-east-1, model:rw-large-16k-v2, runtime:dedicated-pool-3

alice_support: Observability shows a cluster of similar requests around the same millisecond window. Are you doing any client-side batching or retries?

dan_customer: No batching on our side, single request per user action. Latency is fine. We did see more 2026-03-12 14:02:xx spikes, but nothing major.

carol_platform: I'm seeing continuous-batching behavior on the runtime: multiple small requests were coalesced into a batch. Because some had identical prefixes, the KV prefix cache served parts for some requests, but the runtime still executed compute for the batched prefix that got materialized once. This can cause metered token increments that exceed per-request served tokens.

bob_billing: To add: when a batch contains N requests, shared prefix computation may count once for the batch but internal accounting attributes compute usage differently depending on whether KV hits avoided attention work or whether cache warming executed. TL;DR: cache hits reduce served tokens but billing counts the model compute that happened during batching and cache warm-ups.

alice_support: For this specific req_20260312_9f3a I pulled the metering log snippet:
```
metered_tokens: 780
served_tokens: 512
batch_id: b_20260312_14_02_17
kv_cache_hit_ratio: 0.42
cache_warmup_compute_tokens: 310
```
That cache_warmup_compute_tokens explains a big part of the delta.

dan_customer: So we're paying for work that didn't produce output? Feels unfair. Any way to reduce this?

carol_platform: Totally valid. Options:
- Use a per-request "no-batch" flag (trade throughput for per-request billing delta) if you want strict 1:1 billing. Example header: `x-redwood-no-batching: true`.
- Lower batch timeout in config for Dedicated/private deployments if you control the pool.
- Tune prefix caching TTLs or pre-warm the cache for high-traffic prefixes to avoid warmups during traffic spikes.
- We can also filter out cache-warmup accounting for invoice adjustments in exceptional cases (requires billing review).

eric_account: @dan_customer I can work up a one-time invoice credit if this looks like a cache-warmup anomaly during your rollout. Would you like us to do that while you implement one of the mitigations above? :handshake:

dan_customer: Appreciate it. Yes please request the credit and we'll test `x-redwood-no-batching` in staging. Can you confirm the header format?

alice_support: Header is `x-redwood-no-batching: true`. Putting @carol_platform and @bob_billing on the follow-up. I'll attach our tracing for the whole 14:02 window to the ticket.

carol_platform: Follow-up note for engineers: we should add a clearer breakdown in the UI (per-request cache-warmup compute) + a flag in the API response that marks tokens counted due to cache warmup/batch materialization. Filing infra ticket INF-10293.

bob_billing: Filed BILL-7731 to consider automated credits filter for warmup spikes.

eric_account: I'll open the credit case and loop you (dan_customer) in the billing ticket.

dan_customer: Thanks everyone. Will test the header and report back. :rocket:
